content: Magnesium hydroxide is an antacid approved by the FDA for use as a saline laxative and for the treatment of acid-related conditions such as heartburn, sour stomach, and acid indigestion. It is commonly associated with adverse reactions like hypermagnesemia. For adults and children aged 12 years and older, the recommended dosage for occasional constipation relief is 2 to 4 tablespoons, taken with a full glass (8 ounces) of liquid. This typically produces a bowel movement within 30 minutes to 6 hours. For heartburn, sour stomach, or acid indigestion, the dosage is 1 to 3 teaspoons with water, up to 4 times daily. However, no more than 12 teaspoons should be taken within 24 hours, and the maximum dosage should not be used for more than 2 weeks. For pediatric patients, children aged 6 to under 12 years should take 1 to 2 tablespoons, while children aged 2 to under 6 years should take 1 to 3 teaspoons. For children under 2 years, a doctor should be consulted before use. Magnesium hydroxide should be used cautiously in individuals with kidney disease, those on a magnesium-restricted diet, or those experiencing stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or a sudden change in bowel habits lasting more than 2 weeks. It is important to consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if taking other medications, as antacids and laxatives may interact with certain prescription drugs. Laxatives should be taken at least 2 hours before or after other medications to avoid interference with drug absorption. When used as an antacid, magnesium hydroxide may have a laxative effect. If rectal bleeding occurs or there is no bowel movement after use, discontinue the product and consult a doctor, as these may indicate a serious condition. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should seek medical advice before using this medication. There is limited information available regarding the contraindications, clinical trial experience, drug interactions, and pharmacological properties of magnesium hydroxide. Additionally, there is no specific FDA guidance on its use during pregnancy, labor and delivery, nursing, or in pediatric, geriatric, gender-specific, racial, renal-impaired, hepatic-impaired, or immunocompromised populations. Magnesium hydroxide is administered orally. Each 5 mL teaspoon contains 165 mg of magnesium and 2 mg of sodium. It should be stored at room temperature and protected from freezing. Shake the product well before use, and always take it with a full glass of liquid. It can be taken as a single or divided dose. If an overdose is suspected, contact the National Poison Help hotline (1-800-222-1222) immediately. There is limited information on the effects of alcohol interaction with magnesium hydroxide, so it is advisable to consult a doctor regarding alcohol consumption while using this medication. Magnesium hydroxide is marketed under the brand name MAGNESIUM HYDROXIDE®. There is limited information on look-alike drug names for this product.
